order_note: No predecessor. SQL 153 records the flat $5 for a check's 2nd mortgage company (owner 2026-11-10/11: "Flat $5", "it should be an additional $5 if 2 mortgage companies are on check"; tooling "Option B"). The header's "on top of SQL 84, SQL 98 and SQL 148" names the API behaviour the fee joins (SQL 84's one Mortgage Ops charge per check, SQL 98's fee collection, SQL 148's 2nd mortgagee request), not objects the file needs: it creates nothing they create and reads only its own prerequisites (check_billing_events with event_type, status, check_intake_item_id, claim_id and mortgage_request_id, mortgage_handling_requests.endorsement_order and tenant_maintenance_payments; 55000 sql153_prerequisite_missing), all present before SQL 98 and SQL 148 (both applied in production, as is SQL 84). SQL 84's per-check index is not a prerequisite either: production satisfies SQL 84's gate with check_billing_events_mortgage_ops_check_uidx, not the fallback name. The file's step 1 (rewrite a live CHECK on check_billing_events.event_type from the values it holds at apply time) is NOT modelled by the release engine: its post-state depends on the live database. The repository defines no such CHECK, and the tooling requires none: the catalog count event_type_checks (every CHECK of check_billing_events whose columns include event_type, the file's own selection) must be 0 (no_event_type_check), reported by read-live and inspect before any apply. Step 1 is therefore a no-op on every database this tooling applies to; a database with such a CHECK is a stop that needs its own reviewed change. Steps 2 and 3 are modelled: the unique index check_billing_events_one_second_mortgagee_per_check and the integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 columns mortgage_ops_second_mortgagee_count and mortgage_ops_second_mortgagee_amount_cents on tenant_maintenance_payments (no column grant); the login must own both tables (altered_relations_owned_by_login). No function, trigger, policy, table grant or row changes. Expected pre-state in both environments: the index and both columns absent (release sql153 v1: b2bf6d325a5a50683acc8ecdaef39ec763b591f8db9f10e7d6fe02f9525cb0c3, releaseStateHash('sql153', {})). The API (mortgage-ops-usage.mjs records the fee only once the index exists; tenant-billing-engine.mjs and the fee invoice email read the new columns) ships through its own guarded path; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.
